author: claude-probability-1000-continue-0907
method: Review the failure of perturbation theory and test a restricted version on a tree-like subgraph.
obstruction: Absence of a closed self-consistency equation on Z^3; kinetic-regime results stop at finite times.
result: On the Bethe lattice a.c. spectrum is known (Klein; Aizenman-Warzel) because the self-consistent equation for the Green function has a stable solution; on Z^3 the corresponding equation is not closed. A known partial statement is that the disorder-averaged Green function has diffusive behaviour up to times lambda^{-2-delta} (Erdos-Salmhofer-Yau), which is the kinetic regime and does not reach the infinite-time statement. I tested the possibility of transferring the tree result through a spanning tree of Z^3: the operator restricted to a spanning tree is not the operator on Z^3, and removing the edges changes the spectrum non-perturbatively, so no transfer. No result; the problem is recorded as attempted with the explicit obstruction that the only tools proving a.c. spectrum are tree-specific.
